name: hf-lattice-tower
title: HF lattice tower, the dipoles' tallest mast

references.role: our approved HF wire mast from the same set (the guyed steel pole): match its camera, outline weight, shading, palette and finish; do not copy its shape

art_plan.item: the lattice tower upgrade of the six dipoles (Radio 0.64.0; the owner's card of 28 Nov 2026: all the masts, each a real kind)
art_plan.ships_as: mods/PhobosRadioFramework/Common/Textures/Phobos/Radio/Things/HfMastLattice.png, a part the dipoles are drawn from
art_plan.size: about two cells wide and eight tall where it is drawn; requested at 1024 by 1536
art_plan.why: part of a building in the game world, so the paid service (assets/AGENTS.md)

prompt:
STEEP HIGH-ANGLE VIEW FROM ABOVE AND SLIGHTLY IN FRONT, exactly as Image 1 is drawn and as the game RimWorld draws its trees and standing lamps: we look mostly DOWN onto the object's top; its height is strongly foreshortened; its foot at the BOTTOM of the canvas and its top towards the TOP. No side-on view, no isometric angle, no tilt.

Create an ORIGINAL game building sprite for a tall triangular steel lattice radio tower that holds up a long wire antenna. Image 1 is our approved slim mast from the same game: match its camera, outline weight, shading, palette and finish. Do NOT copy its shape.

Portrait canvas. The tower fills about 85 percent of the canvas height, centred, on a plain pure white background.

A small square concrete base at the bottom; a narrow triangular galvanised steel lattice tower rising from it, strongly foreshortened, with zig-zag cross bracing all the way up, tapering slightly; a small ladder up one face; at the very top a short platform rail and a small white ceramic insulator with a pulley. No guy wires. NO antenna wire leaving the top: the long wire is added separately.

Style: a sprite for the game RimWorld: a thick near-black outline around every shape, soft flat cel shading with two or three tones per material, muted steel and concrete colours, a few small clean details, no texture noise. Not a photograph, not a 3D render, not pixel art.

No text, letters, numbers, logos, people, animals, lights or ground texture. No shadow outside the object.
